Let \(CD=x\).

Since \(\triangle APB\) is equilateral, \(AP=AB=18\).  
Since \(\triangle CRD\) is equilateral, \(RD=CD=x\).

At \(B\), the exterior equilateral triangles on \(AB\) and \(BC\) make \(\angle PBQ=90^\circ\), with \(BP=18\) and \(BQ=24\). Thus
\[
PQ=\sqrt{18^2+24^2}=30.
\]

At \(C\), similarly \(\angle QCR=90^\circ\), with \(CQ=24\) and \(CR=x\). Thus
\[
QR=\sqrt{24^2+x^2}=\sqrt{x^2+576}.
\]

Now
\[
P(APQRD)=AP+PQ+QR+RD+DA
=18+30+\sqrt{x^2+576}+x+DA.
\]
Also
\[
P(ABCD)=AB+BC+CD+DA=18+24+x+DA=42+x+DA.
\]
Given \(P(APQRD)=P(ABCD)+32\),
\[
48+x+DA+\sqrt{x^2+576}=74+x+DA.
\]
Thus
\[
\sqrt{x^2+576}=26.
\]
So
\[
x^2+576=676 \implies x^2=100 \implies x=10.
\]

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
